title: Resonant Bodies — Physical Modeling Synth
description: Pluck, strike, and loop four physically-modeled instrument bodies, then bounce your loop to a real WAV.
concept: Resonant Bodies is a tiny physical-modeling instrument lab. Every note is synthesized from scratch by exciting a bank of tuned resonant filters — a real modal-synthesis technique, not a sample or oscillator. Choose between String, Bar, Membrane and Plate bodies (each with its own overtone ratios and decay character), shape them with damping, brightness, size, strike position and mallet hardness, then play them from an on-screen or computer keyboard. A built-in loop pedal records what you play and lets you export the loop as a downloadable WAV.
features: 4 physically-modeled instrument bodies — String, Bar, Membrane, Plate — each a real bank of tuned resonant modes excited by a shaped noise burst
6 live shape parameters: damping, brightness, size/pitch, strike position, mallet hardness, reverb
Loop pedal: record what you play, auto-loop it, pause/resume, and save/load named loops
Bounce the current loop to a real downloadable 16-bit WAV file, re-synthesized deterministically
Save/load named instrument presets plus autosave of the last session, all in localStorage

interaction.mouse: Click a body to select it, drag sliders to shape the sound, click piano keys to play.
interaction.click: Record/Play/Clear/Export the loop pedal; Save/Load named presets and loops.
interaction.touch: Piano keys and all controls respond to touch via Pointer Events.
interaction.keyboard: Play notes with the A S D F G H J K L ; row (with W E T Y U O P for sharps).
